title: Getting started
summary: Choose React or Preact, register your routes, and mount the provider.

sections.title: Install
sections.body: Install the router and the framework you use. Framework peers are optional; choosing React does not install Preact. Smolter’s Vite plugin uses its own pinned stable TypeScript 6 compiler API (typescript-compiler) for typed prefetch selection. Your application can keep TypeScript 7; no compiler downgrade or peer installation is required. The compiler does not enter browser bundles.
sections.code:
pnpm add @kasperrt/smolter react react-dom
# Or: pnpm add @kasperrt/smolter preact
# With Smolter’s Vite plugin:
pnpm add -D vite typescript

sections.title: Define the data
sections.body: Put browser reads in clientLoader.ts. Replace this array with a request to your API when needed.

sections.title: Render the result
sections.body: Re-export the loader from the route module. The type-only import connects useLoaderData to its return type.

sections.title: Register a route
sections.body: Keep the data handler beside the page. defineRoute retains its handler types. Manual routes use the first matching pattern, so put static paths before dynamic paths.

sections.title: Render
sections.body: Create the router outside render. RouterProvider loads the current route; Routes renders its view. Mount App with React’s createRoot or Preact’s render, then open /tasks.

sections.title: Working examples
sections.body: Use these examples alongside the guides. Each pairs a working UI with route registration and its loader/action source.
